two ounces of turpentine, two ounces of marjoram, one pint of oil;
pound and sift the castoreum, then unite it with the rest, and
use it.
Treatment of the feet of animals. Into a new pot
put three pints of oil, and put fresh green lizards into the oil,
about two or even three, and, covering the pot, boil it,
so that the lizards are thoroughly cooked in the oil, and, removing their
bones, add six ounces of ground bitumen, half a pint of liquid pitch,
and two pounds of old pig-fat, and, boiling all these together
well, use it, anointing the hoof. This will make,
as far as possible, the foot of the animal harder.
Another, by Hippocrates: grind together leaven, salt, red ochre, and egg, with vinegar,
and use it.
Another: three ounces of resin, three ounces of wax, one ounce of turpentine,
two pounds of lard, two ounces of oil, four pints of vetch, a mixture of vinegar,
two ounces of hemlock, half a cotyla of pitch, two pounds of old salt-fish,
one cotyla of honey; grind the salt-fish together with these,
and, putting it into a mortar-bowl, use it.
Another: enough old olive-lees and old cedar-oil, and
old lard with wine and quicklime-lye, ground thoroughly...
Boil each of these, and, boiling it sufficiently with the olive-lees, use it.
Another: six ounces of garlic, four ounces of sulfur, six ounces of iris, two pounds of pig-lard; boil in vinegar and use it.

By Hierocles, for the same: one and a half ounces of spurge, one ounce of castoreum, two ounces of bdellium, two ounces each of galbanum, opopanax, and litharge, six ounces of bitumen, four ounces of frankincense-manna, six ounces of roasted resin, two ounces of ammoniac incense.
Apsyrtus, against those discharging fluid from the nostrils: mix butter or oil with fish-sauce, and drench through the nostrils, then, tying the head down to the feet, let it graze.

Theomnestus, against fluid discharged through the nostrils from chilling: draw blood from the temples, so that, by this outlet, you loosen the areas around the head, and all the phlegm hardened in the head by the chilling may be dissolved and slip down through the nostrils. Before the bloodletting, one must pour hot oil over the crown of the animal's head; for this will assist the loosening. Let it be drenched with lees-spiced wine through the mouth and through the nostrils, so that the heat of the pepper, loosening the blockage, may induce hawking, through which the troublesome matter must necessarily be expelled. And if, once these are applied, the affliction is not resolved, mix one drachm of opopanax, six drachms of castoreum, one drachm of laser-resin, and one Italian pint of dark wine or spiced wine, and drench once, and you will marvel.
Another, by Pelagonius. The moistness of the nostrils

varies. If, then, the discharge is clear, it is part of everyday habit, and there is nothing wrong with it. But if it is thicker and whiter, it comes down from the brain. If reddish and thin, it comes from old chilling, and thus fevers are foreshadowed by it. If fattier and frothy, it is sent up from the lung. If denser, it descends from the glands. These are the things one must observe and commit to memory.
Against those bringing up pus through the nostrils.
Grind one ounce of male frankincense with one Attic cotyla of wine, and, warming it, drench through both nostrils, and after this fumigate with bay-leaves.
Apsyrtus, against seiriasis: six ounces of verdigris, enough quicklime.
A poultice for swelling: barley-flour, lard, enough vinegar.

Against 'phazaina' (a skin eruption): you will disperse 'phazaina' thus: one pound of quicklime, one pound of ivy-flower, one pint of hazelnuts, one pound of mastic-oil, two pounds of old lard, one pound of bean-flower. Grind these into one and anoint the place.
Another astringent: six ounces of verdigris, two pounds each of chalcitis, misy, and acacia, one pint of pomegranate-rind, three pints of vinegar.

Against 'drakontia' (a serpent-like skin ailment): you will recognize 'drakontia' thus: blisters arise over the whole body and break open, which you will treat thus: take rue, roses, and castoreum, and, mixing them into one, first burn through its blisters, and then anoint, until it becomes healthy.
Three ounces each of burnt chalcitis, cave-myrrh, aromatic myrrh, and aloe, one pound of honey; grind these in a mortar, and anoint the wound.

Hierocles' composition of an adhesive plaster: two ounces of frankincense, one and a half pints of boiled must, three ounces of mastic, one pint of rose-oil, one and a half pints of fine flour, one pint of bulbs, fifteen eggs, twenty-five snails.

Pelagonius' composition of a fatty ointment: six ounces of litharge, two pounds of wax, three ounces of white-lead, four ounces of male frankincense, two ounces of deer-marrow, two pounds of oil; mix all these in wine and boil, and use it.
Apsyrtus' pitch-ointment: one and a half pounds of roasted resin, two pounds of dry pitch, one pound of wax, two pounds of oil, two ounces of melilot, half an ounce of wine.
The ointment of Azanites: two ounces of dry pitch, three ounces of wax, six ounces of pig-fat, three ounces of unwashed wool-grease, five ounces of pine-resin, six ounces of bull-fat.

The great ointment of Azanites, against all malignant conditions: five ounces of dry pitch, one pound of bull-fat, six ounces of old pig-fat, two and a half pounds of wax, six ounces of unwashed wool-grease, two pounds of pine-resin, three ounces of deer-marrow, six ounces of bird-fat, six ounces of turpentine, three ounces of goose-fat, three ounces of galbanum, six ounces of butter.
The green ointment: two ounces of verdigris, two pounds of resin, three ounces of oil in winter, one ounce in summer, three ounces of wax, enough water.
The 'beloved' ointment: one pound of wax, two pounds of unsalted pig-fat, one pound of roasted resin, four ounces of frankincense, four ounces of myrrh,
two pounds of roasted sorrel; wrap the sorrel in paper, boil it in warm ash, and, grinding it, add it to the wax-salve.
The 'little Aphrodite': one pound of bull-fat, one pound of fresh pig-fat, six ounces of goat-fat, six ounces of sheep-fat, one pound of pine-resin, one pound of wax; melt and strain, and use it.
The 'moist-side' ointment: two pounds of wax, four ounces of white-lead, four ounces of starch, three ounces of litharge; melt and use it.

The ointment made with mandrake-juice: two pounds each of old pig-fat, Brittany pitch, wax, roasted resin, and common oil, three ounces each of litharge, white-lead, and split alum, two ounces each of misy, gall-nuts, and chalcitis, one ounce each of poppy-juice, opopanax, liver-colored aloe, myrrh, and frankincense, three ounces of mandrake-juice, enough very sharp vinegar; put the meltable ingredients into a mortar, and, taking them up, add the dry ones, and make a paste. And if you wish to dilute it, do it thus: one pound of the remedy, one pound of wax, one pound of Brittany pitch, six pounds of common oil.

Hierocles' fumigated 'barbara' preparation: one pound each of Judaean bitumen, dry pitch, wax, and resin, two ounces of turpentine, one ounce of litharge, one and a half ounces of white-lead, two ounces of frankincense-manna, two ounces of opopanax, one ounce of myrrh, three ounces of oil, enough vinegar. With this, he said [gap] he had healed all wounds of solid-hoofed animals (once it has been thoroughly clarified beforehand, applied together with vinegar-brine, or dissolving it with wax and rose-oil).

Apsyrtus' preparation of soaked-grain feeds, which the Cappadocians give to thin horses: three modii of barley, three pints of broad beans, eight pints of chickpeas, eight pints of kidney-beans, two pints of vetch, two pints of wine; soak these in the evening, and, mixing them in the morning and drying them a little, give a half-modius, army-measure, in the evening and a half-modius in the morning, so that the animal eats one army-modius daily. If, then, the animal is very thin, it will eat the aforesaid for twenty-one consecutive days; if not, fifteen or seven. On the days it eats, let it not go out of the stable, but drink there. The Syrians add to this mixture one pint of pine-nuts and one pint of raisins, and give it for seven days to a horse standing in a dark stable with a very dry floor.

A remedy against various afflictions, and, by experience, for driving shadows out of stables: one ounce of magnet-stone, two ounces of 'Solomon's stone,' one ounce of all-heal, six ounces of bitumen, one ounce of sulfur, six ounces of hog's-fennel; mix these together with resin and turpentine, take it up, and use it.

Eumelus, against nausea: nausea, and sluggishness around feeding, is stopped by about two cyathi of ground black cumin, mixed with three pints of oil and one pint of wine, and given. Or grind one head of garlic with half a pint of wine, and give through a horn.
Eumelus, against pain of the joints: bloodletting is exceptionally beneficial. And if the joints ache, or become suppurative, treat it thus: chop pounded iris, frankincense-
meal, red gall-nut, opopanax-root, and birthwort, one ounce of each, and use it.
Against 'glossis' (a tongue swelling): prick the vein under the tongue, and apply as a poultice vinegar with laser-resin and bran, and give feed and lukewarm water as drink.
Hippocrates, on a cut tongue: if the tongue is cut, boil a gall-nut with dark wine, and, taking it up, use it, or chop centaury and apply it.
Another: Pelagonius, against a cut tongue: knead iris with honey, and apply to the tongue, washing it off afterward with wine. After one day, use the same method again, until complete healing.
Eumelus, against those suffering from gum-boils: draw blood from the upper part of the cheek, and have the gums pricked, and thus rub them with salt, until it becomes healthy.

If the anus suffers a prolapse: if the anus prolapses, foment it with oil and sheep-fat and lukewarm water, and push it gently inward, then grind roasted resin with the aforesaid ingredients and apply it to the anus.

Against afflictions in the anus: if the affliction around the anus is found to be extensive, from much irritation or itching, you will treat it thus: take the five-leaved herb (cinquefoil) and fifteen heads of garlic, and, grinding these, make pastilles, which take up with six ounces of honey and one pint of oil. Then insert them through the left nostril. Or give a preliminary drench of two pints of dripping lye with half a pint of wine.
On a horse's defecation: if a horse cannot pass dung, take soda and four eggs and four cotylae of oil and four cotylae of hot water, and pour it into the anus with a syringe.
On a cut anus: boil frankincense in fragrant wine and apply, then grind the ash of boiled iris very fine, and, anointing with oil, sprinkle it on, boiling this too in hot water.

Eumelus' purging of the belly: purge the belly thus: enough wild-cucumber root, six grammes of laser-resin, four pints of honey, eight pints of hot water; grind these and warm them, and insert through the anus, and use this generously, until the remedy runs through all the internal parts, and let it walk about, until the belly is purged. As a drink, give honey-water, adding soda and hellebore.

Theomnestus' exposition of purgative remedies: slaughter a puppy that has just begun to eat, singe it and boil it, then throw away all its entrails, and, mixing the broth with one pint of fragrant wine and one pint of honey, make the whole broth, straining it through linen, so that the bones remain in the pot, measuring six cotylae, and drench the animal with one of these, for three days, two cotylae at a time, adding a handful of soda. And if there is no puppy, boil one shoulder-cut of a very fat pig together with the thigh, and, adding the same ingredients, use it. We ourselves have also used white spurge and fine birthwort and fine centaury, boiling these and straining them, and mixing in honey,
we drench, making a broth as described for the pig.
On purging: if it is not purged by the usual means, or has some other illness of the belly, soak spurge and lard in wine-and-oil, and drench through the mouth, or chop cabbage-leaves and apply.

Eumelus, against displacement of the back: soak barley-groats in wine and oil and apply. And if it produces a lung-like growth, cut it deeply, and, mixing horse-dung with vinegar and oil and ground unslaked salt, apply to the wound, and you will cure it.
For removing hard knots: mix equal parts of chalcitis-flower, verdigris, litharge-scum, soda, salt, and vinegar together, and, grinding them, use it.
Eumelus, for making animals lay aside their wildness: give a bird's feather to swallow, in whatever manner you wish.

Against a roughened throat: if the animal's throat is roughened, and does not discharge pus, dissolve tragacanth in water, and grind six ounces of Rhodian glue in a pound and a half of wine, and drench.
A softening remedy: six staters of wax, one cotyla of oil, three staters of Colophonian resin; mix these together and boil, store in a vessel, and use it.
A sneeze-inducing remedy: burn soda, and pound and sift soapwort, white pepper, Illyrian iris, and cow-wheat, and blow it into the nostrils.
A caustic remedy: four ounces of orpiment, three ounces of litharge-scale, two ounces of black hellebore; chop these with dried figs and mix with oil, and use it.

An aromatic horse-remedy: three ounces each of cassia and cinnamon, four ounces of ginger, one pound of costus, three ounces of cardamom, six ounces of aromatic reed, six ounces of camel-thorn flower, one pound of saffron-dregs, one ounce of saffron, four ounces of cave-myrrh, four ounces of wood-cinnamon, six ounces of white pepper, one pound each of opopanax, gentian, and Illyrian iris, six ounces each of birthwort and peony.

Hierocles' aromatic preparation: eight ounces each of leaf, costus, cardamom, spikenard, cassia, and camel-thorn flower, six ounces each of iris and cardamom, one pint of melilot, one pint of hyssop, eight ounces each of Celtic nard, parsley, and wood-balsam, six ounces each of laser-resin, aromatic reed, and Cnidian grain, one pint of marjoram, an equal amount of dried roses, six ounces each of birthwort, gentian, licorice, hog's-fennel, centaury, saffron, pepper, and tragacanth, one hundred dates, five pints of honey, ten pints of oil, one hundred fifty eggs, one pint of Megarian first-quality wine.

Preparation of a horse fatigue-liniment: one ounce each of honey and wax, one ounce of litharge, half an ounce of black copper; pour these in a third at a time, stirring, until it becomes red, adding one cyathus of vinegar, then, mixing in carob together with oleander-herb, boiling it in water, and pounding the herb with lard. This works the same on humans.

Hierocles' preparation of a horse fatigue-liniment: four ounces each of opopanax, galbanum, castoreum, ammoniac gum, spurge, pellitory, and turpentine, six ounces each of marjoram and deer-marrow, four ounces each of myrrh and pompholyx, five pounds of wax, eight pints of oil.

Hippasius of Elis' compound: sheep-lard, litharge, oil, wine; take all these up and use it for ulcerations and treatment of fresh swellings. This works exceptionally well also for spinal problems in cattle.
Hippocrates' adhesive plaster: mix enough boiled must, tragacanth, saffron, pine-nuts, chalcitis, and eggs, and use it.

Hierocles' adhesive remedy: two or three ounces of frankincense, two ounces of mastic, three ounces of cumin, one and a half pints of boiled must, one pint of rose-oil, one and a half pints of bulbs, fifteen eggs.
The same author's preparation of a four-drug remedy: six ounces each of round birthwort, gentian, bdellium, and bay-berries.
To treat vitiligo without a scalpel: pound mullein, and apply as a poultice to the affected place. Then pound groundsel, and apply as a poultice to the remaining place, and bind it.

Fleabane, effective against burns and especially against sinew-wounds: three ounces of galbanum, six ounces of resin-drippings, six ounces of roasted resin, three ounces of turpentine, one pound each of wax, oil, and fleabane-juice; boil the oil with the juice, until they unite. Then melt the meltable ingredients and mix them in, and use it.

Preparation of a fatty remedy: five pounds of litharge, three pounds of resin-drippings, seven pounds of white-lead, eight ounces of sarcocolla, four ounces of frankincense-manna, thirteen pounds of white wax, ten pounds of fresh lard, seven pounds of rose-oil, fifty eggs, enough old wine.
Pelagonius' preparation of a fatty remedy: take equal parts of litharge, white-lead, and male frankincense, grind them, and, adding saffron, oil, and enough honey, use it.

If the cartilage of the nose is split: when the cartilage of the nose is split, and a quantity of blood is discharged that cannot be stopped, apply a small sponge with vinegar and frankincense-meal, and bind it, until a scar forms. Treat the wound with a wound-plaster.
If a horse begins to gnaw at its own foot: mix moist dog-dung with very sharp vinegar, and apply as a poultice continually.

A dry compound for a four-horse team (tethrippon): one ounce of Pontic sweet-flag, three ounces of myrrh, six ounces of pepper, two ounces of saffron-dregs, three ounces of Illyrian iris, one ounce of hyssop, two ounces each of emollient, garlic, and Pontic salt.

On giving vegetables. If, in the winter season, you wish to give an animal vegetables, boil the vegetable carefully the day before, and make it like troches, putting in oil and ground salt and parsley and cumin on that day; on the following day, make the seasoning drier by adding lard, and give it.

On giving lard. It is an excellent remedy, in the winter season, to give the animal, against internally-arising afflictions, lard with liquid pitch and oil; in summer, lard with honey and butter and leeks and rose-oil. Let the animal take this often.

Preparation of the four-horse-team remedy called 'coudrigarium': Syrian or Indian nard, Sicilian saffron, cave-myrrh, camel-thorn flower, black pepper, white pepper, black cassia, germander, Celtic nard, cinnamon, Indian onions, Pontic agaric, male frankin-
cense, white iris, calamint, Pontic laser-resin, gentian, dry parsley, cassia-tube; pound and sift all these in equal weight, as seems good to you, and use it.

Signs of a paralytic affliction. The signs in paralytic cases are these: misshapen and drooping lips, a tongue deadened by the affliction, one of the eyes smaller, one ear drooping. You will treat it, then, thus: first, having scraped the lips, use this ointment: six ounces each of old oil, bitumen, and pine-resin, one pound of ammoniac gum, one ounce of galbanum, an equal amount of propolis, six ounces of frankincense-manna, one ounce of deer-marrow; boil all these together and use it.
A poultice for the hip: boil equal parts of vinegar and water with resin, and add barley-flour, so as to have the consistency of a poultice; apply this hot to the affected places.

Against every swelling, if it is not yet hot or inflamed. This also works on humans: six ounces each of wax, pitch, Colophonian resin, and ammoniac gum, two ounces of pig-fat, one ounce each of soda, quicklime, bulb, and dove-dung, six ounces of cedar-tar, a little water and myrrh-oil.

A plaster against all malignant wounds and spreading ulcers and chronic shin-sores and abscesses, especially those near the anus: equal parts of white-lead, litharge, mastic, henbane-juice, and myrtle-oil. Grind the white-lead and the litharge together with the mastic beforehand, adding the myrtle-oil and the henbane-
juice drop by drop, take it up, and, making a plaster, store it in a lead vessel. And if it hardens over time, soften it again with myrtle-oil and a little wine, and use it.

Against a horse foundered on barley, and fallen, and unable to walk or rise: gather wild-fig leaves, chop them carefully, and put them into lukewarm water, and, straining through a sieve, and putting it into a horn, give it to drink twice or even three times, and, forcing it, make it move about, and you will have it healthy.

The plaster made with dittany: one hundred drachms of litharge, fifty drachms of Colophonian resin, twenty-five drachms of wax, sixteen drachms each of ammoniac incense and birthwort, twelve drachms each of frankincense-manna and galbanum, eight drachms each of verdigris, burnt copper, dittany, aloe, and propolis, six drachms each of copper-scale, diphryges, and gentian, fourteen ounces of oil. Boil the litharge and the oil until it no longer stains. Then add the verdigris and boil likewise, then the resin and the sifted ammoniac gum, and boil, then the diphryges, and boil again, and then add the wax, and, taking it from the fire, add the galbanum softened together with the propolis, and boil a little. Afterward, warming it, add the aloe, the frankincense-manna, the dittany, the birthwort, and the gentian, and, if it stains, boil over a gentle fire. It is also good to add a little water, so that the litharge does not burn.
A plaster, applied by various methods against every affliction, and effective against old and fresh

sores: nine ounces of good oil, one pound each of Judaean bitumen, fatty wax, roasted resin, and clean pitch, ten drachms each of litharge, white-lead, and scraped verdigris, four drachms each of split alum, blue vitriol, chalcitis, and saffron, sixteen drachms each of ammoniac incense, male frankincense, liver-colored aloe, cave-myrrh, and Theban poppy-juice, enough sharp vinegar.

The painless plaster, dispersing the excess of inflammations: four ounces each of asphodel-juice and 'perdikion'-juice, three ounces each of wax, fresh butter, lard, quicklime, and calf-marrow, twelve drachms each of soda-froth, Cimolian earth, burnt wine-lees, and soda, twelve drachms of boiled glue from meal, twelve drachms of chopped and boiled melilot-seed, three pounds of good oil; prepare and use it.

Gregory's troche for dysentery: one ounce each of starch and acacia, one and a half ounces of lycium, six ounces each of saffron, myrrh, and frankincense, three ounces of poppy-juice; grind all these carefully, each separately, then, uniting them, grind again with a decoction of roses, or willow, or fresh myrtle, for two days in a mortar, then dry it and use it, adding some of the said decoction. And if
the affliction is chronic, one must first flush the intestine with willow-juice.
And if what is discharged is blood-tinged, add hematite-stone to the troche and use it. From this same troche one can also make elongated suppositories.
It works also when anointed on the navel, the stomach, and the belly.

A stomach-plaster: two ounces each of groundsel, nettle-seed, mastic, and wax, one ounce of honey, two ounces of scammony; dissolve the wax with the honey, and, making the rest into a dry compound, sprinkle it on and anoint, and it moves the belly.
A three-part binding poultice: pound and sift willow- or pine-bark, and burn and grind the horn of a running deer, and grind oats, and unite them together, and use it on clean, proud-flesh wounds.
An emollient effective against everything: two pounds of wax, [gap] of alum, one ounce of litharge, six ounces of pine-resin, six ounces of ammoniac gum, six ounces of sulfur.

Another, seeded emollient: one and a half pounds of wax, six ounces of dill, three ounces of southernwood-seed, four ounces of calamint-seed, six ounces of fine bay-berries, one pound of ammoniac gum, six ounces of settled resin, six ounces of celery. Put these into a pot and boil. And when they are boiled, pour them into a small bowl of cold water, and empty it out, and, taking it out, use it.

An ointment: two pounds of wax, four pounds of pine-resin, six ounces of ammoniac gum, three ounces of opopanax, three ounces of galbanum, two ounces of saffron-dregs, three ounces of deer-marrow, mastic-oil
three ounces, six ounces of old oil, an equal amount of bay-oil, three ounces of myrrh.

A barbarian emollient: one pound of wax, six ounces of roasted resin, six ounces of hemlock, six ounces of Judaean bitumen, six ounces of propolis, four ounces of galbanum, three ounces of opopanax, six ounces of oil, half a pint of vinegar, pig-fat.
A wound-emollient: six ounces of honey, three ounces each of aloe, chalcitis, and myrrh.
Another: nine ounces of honey, [gap] of chalcitis, one ounce of good roasted barley, six [gap] of myrrh; combine all these in a mortar, grind them smooth, and use it.
Another: three cyathi of vinegar, one pound of alum, six ounces of verdigris; use these.
An adhesive plaster against the sinews: one ounce of frankincense-manna, fifteen snails, fifteen Megarian bulbs, half a pint of fine flour.

A cold poultice: one pint of fine flour, one ounce of frankincense-manna, six ounces of pitch, enough old wine; put these into a wash-basin and knead. This works well for what has been dislocated, and for other afflictions.
A fiery poultice: one pint of frankincense-manna, one ounce of red ochre, half a pint of vinegar; this works well against inflammations.

Another: six ounces of lion-fat, six ounces of female-cow fat, six ounces each of wax, turpentine-resin, cassia, saffron-dregs, and propolis, three ounces each of sulfur, soda, and aloe, one pound of bay-berries.

An ointment: three ounces each of galbanum, propolis, old oil, bitter almonds, soda-flower, and opopanax, two ounces each of ammoniac gum, turpentine-resin, and Assian-stone flower, four ounces of iris-oil, wax, radish-oil, and deer-

marrow; one ounce each of wax, galbanum, ammoniac gum, frankincense, deer-marrow, old oil, and unwashed wool-grease, two ounces each of propolis and turpentine, three ounces each of bdellium, storax, myrrh, opopanax, and cedar-oil.
An ointment: one pound of Tyrrhenian wax, one ounce each of propolis and unwashed wool-grease, three ounces each of old oil and rose-oil, six ounces of pig-fat.

Another ointment: one pound of Tyrrhenian wax, six ounces each of opopanax, rose-oil, henna-oil, and bay-oil, three ounces each of storax and bull-fat, four ounces of unwashed wool-grease, one ounce of goose-fat.
An emollient made from figs: three ounces of figs, six ounces of soda, one ounce each of cypress and galbanum, six ounces each of bull-fat and frankincense-manna.
An ointment: one pound each of wax, unwashed wool-grease, and old oil, three ounces each of opopanax and white-lead, four ounces each of bdellium and storax, six pounds of myrrh.

Preparation of small circular troches: three ounces each of saffron, myrrh, Syrian nard, costus, Illyrian iris, Pontic rhubarb, long pepper, white pepper, camel-thorn flower, parsley, cyperus, and ginger, two ounces each of cinnamon, cassia, cardamom, male frankincense, and sweet-flag, four ounces each of sulfur, spikenard, saffron-dregs, opopanax, iris, knucklebone-seed, carrot, storax, walnut, and pure nard, five ounces of reed, four ounces of gentian.
Titus' eye-salve: one drachm of burnt copper, seven drachms of burnt antimony, five drachms of nard, cassia-
juice one pint, five drachms of saffron, seven drachms of white-lead.

The same author's other eye-salve: one drachm of burnt cadmia, seven drachms of burnt copper, twenty-eight drachms of roasted antimony, three drachms of aloe, an equal amount of celandine-juice, five drachms of prepared white-lead, one drachm of saffron, three drachms of nard, one drachm of vinegar, five drachms of washed acacia, five drachms of myrrh, thirty-six drachms of gum, three pints of wine.
A white, all-purpose wound-poultice: one pound of litharge, two pints of seawater, one pint of oil; put these into a pot and boil until it thickens, and use it for everything.

A plaster for everything: eighteen drachms of turpentine-resin, four drachms of verdigris, two drachms of copper-scale, seven drachms of oak-gall, four drachms of split alum, eighteen drachms of wax, one cyathus of oil, four cyathi of vinegar. Melt the meltable ingredients and pour them over the ground ones. And if it is too liquid, boil until it stains.

A drench against various afflictions: forty grains of pepper, eight drachms of myrrh, four drachms each of costus, sweet-flag, nard, valerian, and carrot, an equal amount of wild ginger, eight drachms of saffron, twelve drachms of cinnamon, four drachms of parsley; pound all these separately, and shape into pastilles with the best honey, a bean's size. This is beneficial against flatulence and against pains in the body, and it also helps those with spleen, liver, and kidney ailments, and it works against headaches and against suspicion of deadly poisons.
A black plaster for everything: litharge,
four drachms, seven drachms of wax, ten cyathi of oil, vinegar,
one drachm; put the wax, the oil, and the vinegar together and
melt them. Then, grinding the litharge, set it aside then and spread it in.
Add one drachm of aloe, four drachms of frankincense-manna, verdigris
one drachm, five drachms of white-lead, nine drachms of ammoniac salt, two drachms of copper-scale, one drachm of galbanum.
